transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm... just here because people told me to come. My family, mostly. They think I'm... well, they don't understand why I can't just let things go. 

It's about my father. He passed away recently. And, look, I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But... I'm a systems analyst. I look at data for a living. When I compare the timestamps on those emails, the missing attachments, and... and just the way certain people in the community completely avoid my questions... it's obvious. Someone is hiding what really happened around his death. But no one wants to hear it.
Do you find yourself thinking about your father's death and the possibility of a cover-up for most of the day?
I mean... I guess I think about it a fair amount. It's hard not to when the pieces don't fit. But... I wouldn't say it's all day. Just... when I'm looking at the files, mostly.
Do you believe that your theory about your father's death is definitely true, even when others, including the hospital, say otherwise?

I mean... yes. I know what I'm looking at. 

The hospital says one thing, my family says another... but the data is right there. The timestamps on those donation emails, the missing attachments... it doesn't just happen like that. And then people in the community just... look away when I ask about it. 

So, yes. Even if they don't want to admit it, I know what the evidence says. It's obvious someone is covering it up.
Do you feel anxious when you're not investigating your father's death?

I wouldn't say anxious, no. 

I mean... I have a job. I work. I just... look into things when I have the time. It's not like I'm sitting around worrying about it all day. I just check the files when I need to. That's all.
Do you feel compelled to keep investigating your father's death?

I wouldn't say compelled. 

I just... look into it when I need to. Like I said. It's not a compulsion, it's just... something I do.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about your father's death?

I don't think so, no. 

I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those emails all line up perfectly. But... I've compared the timestamps myself. I know about the missing attachments. And... you just notice the way certain people in the community avoid my questions. 

It's just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. So, no. I'm not mistaken.
Do you think your belief about your father's death would change if you found evidence contradicting your current theory?

I don't... I don't see how that would happen. 

Like I just said, I've seen the hospital records. I've seen the donation emails. People tell me they line up, but... they don't. I've looked at the timestamps. I know there are missing attachments. And the way people around here just... look away when I ask about it. 

So, I don't know what evidence you mean. It's just... it's obvious what's going on. Someone's hiding it. I don't need to change my mind when I can see it right there.
Do you think other people can see the evidence you've found about your father's death, or do you believe you're the only one who can see it?

I mean... they could see it if they actually looked. 

Like I keep saying, the data is right there. Anyone can see the timestamps don't match, or that the attachments are missing. It's not... I'm not making it up. But everyone else just accepts it when they're told the hospital records and the donation emails line up. They don't want to look closer. Or they just... avoid the topic entirely when I ask. 

So, no. I'm not the only one who *can* see it. I'm just the only one actually looking.
Do you think your life would be significantly impacted if you were to stop investigating your father's death?

Not really. I mean... I still go to work. I handle my projects, pay my bills... I keep my normal routine. It's not like it's taking over everything. 

The only place things get... tense, I guess, is when I bring up my questions about his records with my family, or people in the community. So... I suppose that tension would stop. But my day-to-day wouldn't really change.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death are based on facts or do you feel like you have a special insight that others don't have?

It's based on facts. I don't have... special insight or anything. 

I work with data. I'm just looking at what's there. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, but... they don't. When I compare the timestamps, and look at the missing attachments... and then see the way certain people around here just avoid my questions... 

It's not some special feeling. It's just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. I'm just reading the facts in front of me.
Do you feel that your beliefs about your father's death are causing you significant emotional distress?

I mean... no. Not really. 

I don't know what you mean by significant distress. It's just... something I'm looking into. It doesn't keep me up at night or anything. I just want to know what happened. That's all.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death could be considered unreasonable by others?

I don't know. I guess... maybe. 

I haven't really asked them. People can think what they want, I suppose. I don't really focus on that.
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about your father's death even when you're engaged in other activities?

Not really. I mean... I still do my job just fine. 

When I'm working on a system at the office, I'm focused on that. It doesn't... get in the way of other things, if that's what you're asking. I can put it down when I need to.
Have your investigations into your father's death caused problems in your relationships with family or friends?

I wouldn't call them problems. Work is fine... my performance there has stayed steady. 

With my family, I guess... some of my relatives kind of avoid talking to me lately. They probably just assume I'm going to bring up the records... and what I think was concealed. So they just keep their distance. But I don't really mind.
Do you ever consider the possibility that you might be misinterpreting the data about your father's death?

Not really. I know... I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up. 

But... I look at the data. The timestamps... the missing attachments. And when I ask certain people in the community about it, they just avoid my questions. It's... it's obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened. So, no... I don't think I'm misinterpreting anything.
Can you think of any other possible explanations for the discrepancies you've found in your father's hospital records and donation emails?

No. I mean... I just told you. 

If there was another simple explanation, like a clerical error or something, people wouldn't act the way they do. Everyone keeps saying it all lines up, but... the timestamps don't. The attachments are missing. And when I try to ask people in the community about it, they just avoid me. 

If it was just an innocent mistake, they'd just say so. So... no. It's obvious someone is hiding what really happened. I don't see what else it could be.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would change if someone you trust, like a close family member or a professional, presented you with evidence that contradicts your current theory?

I... I don't know. 

I mean, people already tell me it lines up. They say the records and the emails are fine. But... I see the timestamps. I see what's missing. And when I ask, they just... they don't answer. 

So... if someone brought me "evidence"... I don't know what that would even look like. It's just obvious to me that something is being hidden. I don't think someone else saying otherwise would change what I'm looking at.
Do you feel like you have to keep checking the data about your father's death over and over?

No. Not really. 

I mean... I already know what the data says. I don't need to keep looking at it.
Could you consider that there might be an innocent reason for the discrepancies you've found in your father's hospital records and donation emails?

I... I don't know. 

I mean, I know everyone keeps telling me that everything lines up. The hospital, the emails... they all say it's fine. But... it's just the timestamps. And the attachments that aren't there. 

And then... when I ask people about it, they just... they avoid me. So... no. It just seems obvious that someone is hiding something. I don't see how it could be innocent.
Do you feel like you're spending an excessive amount of time thinking about your father's death compared to other things in your life?

No. Not really. 

I... I still go to work and do my job. I don't just sit around dwelling on it all day. It's just... something I know. So... no, I wouldn't call it excessive.
